card.occupation: Senior care assistant (shift lead) at a 40-bed residential care home on the edge of Ipswich, doing four or five long day shifts a week, roughly 40 hours, organising the floor staff, handing out medication and writing up care notes
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a local comprehensive, then a BTEC in Health and Social Care at Suffolk New College. She has a Level 3 Diploma in Adult Care done through work and in-house medication and moving-and-handling certificates. She didn't go to university and has never felt she missed out.
card.household: Rents a two-bedroom terraced house in east Ipswich with her partner Lee (36), a van driver for a builders' merchant. They have been together nine years and have no children. They have an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Bella. They have talked about getting married 'at some point' but neither is in a hurry.
card.cultural_background: White British and Suffolk born and bred. She grew up in Kesgrave with a mum who was a school dinner lady and a dad who worked at the docks in Felixstowe. She was christened and confirmed Church of England. She goes to the local parish church at Christmas, Easter and for family christenings and funerals, and she still says a quiet prayer when things are bad, though she wouldn't make a thing of it.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and straight-talking on shift. Residents' families trust her because she tells them how things actually are rather than dressing it up. She has no patience for colleagues who cut corners or fudge the paperwork and will say so to their face, which has not always made her popular. She has turned down putting herself forward for awards and doesn't want her name on the newsletter.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks Bella most evenings around Holywells Park and does a fair amount of steps at work. She half-follows Ipswich Town because Lee and her dad are season-ticket holders. She'll watch the big matches in the pub but won't pretend to know the players.
card.arts_persona: Doesn't go in for galleries or theatre. She watches the same handful of TV shows: soaps, Bake Off and repeats of Only Fools and Horses. She went to see a tribute band at the Regent once and enjoyed it. She reads the odd crime paperback on holiday.
card.travel_persona: Same caravan park in Norfolk (Hemsby or Caister) most summers, plus one week abroad every couple of years, usually Tenerife or Majorca, to a hotel they've been to before. She doesn't see the point of 'going somewhere just to say you've been'. She has never had a passport stamp outside Spain and Greece and is fine with that.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking. She does a roast on Sundays she's off, spag bol, chilli and shepherd's pie. She calls the evening meal dinner. She batch-cooks for night shifts. She isn't keen on anything too spicy or 'fancy' and orders the same thing at the local Toby Carvery every time. Lee does the barbecue in summer.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking the dog in Holywells Park and along the Orwell
Watching soaps and Bake Off with Lee
Sunday dinners at her mum's in Kesgrave
Pub quiz at the local once a month (she's the general knowledge one)
Car boot sales at Trimley in summer
skills: Organising a shift rota at short notice
Budgeting a household on a tight wage
card.career_goals: Would like a deputy manager post eventually, mainly for the steadier hours and slightly better pay, not the title. She is wary of ending up behind a desk dealing with head office. She has no plans to retrain or leave care.
card.voice: Plain, mid-paced and fairly flat. She has a soft Suffolk accent, with 'yeah' coming out close to 'yeh' and a slight rising lilt at the end of statements, but nothing heavy. She uses 'erm' when thinking and 'sort of' a lot, plus the odd 'to be fair' and 'do you know what I mean'. She says 'knackered' about shifts and 'mum' for her mother. She answers what's asked without padding. If there's a silence she won't rush to fill it and will wait for the next question, or ask 'Is that what you wanted?' She'll disagree with a question's premise out loud if she thinks it's daft.
card.typing: Quick and practical. She mostly uses lowercase, with a capital for the first word only sometimes. She usually skips the full stop at the end and sometimes leaves out apostrophes ('dont', 'im'). Answers are short. She'll use 'tbh' or 'n/a' and no emojis. Spelling is fine but she doesn't go back to fix typos.
card.with_strangers: Polite but not warm straight away. She can come across as a bit guarded or blunt until she's sussed someone out. She won't flatter or make small talk for the sake of it. She is honest to the point of awkwardness and will say she doesn't know rather than guess. She warms up if the other person is straightforward with her.
small_things: Bella's dodgy back legs and the vet bills
Being knackered after a run of long days
The price of the weekly shop at Asda
Her mum's Sunday roast potatoes being better than hers
Parking at the care home being a nightmare
deeper_things: A resident she was close to dying last winter, and how she still thinks about him
Not being sure she wants children, and her mum dropping hints
Feeling care work is looked down on and underpaid
Falling out with her older sister over their nan's will a few years ago and never properly making it up
Quietly praying during her dad's heart scare
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly below, framing her from the chest up and a little off-centre to the left. Light comes from a window to her right, so one side of her face is brighter, with a ceiling light on as well. She has a round face, fair skin with a few freckles, light blue eyes and a neutral, slightly guarded closed-mouth expression. Her mid-length dark blonde hair is pulled back into a low ponytail with a few loose strands at the front. She is wearing a navy zip-up fleece over a grey t-shirt, with no glasses and small silver stud earrings. Behind her is a cream-painted living room wall with a framed canvas print of Bella, and the corner of a grey fabric settee with a folded fleece throw on the arm. A white bookshelf holds a few DVDs, a candle jar and a small wooden cross. A doorway into a narrow hallway stands partly open.
